_note: MINERVA T1's recovery ladder (docs/recovery.md): the sequencer's telescopes.t1.recovery entry, or a rehearsal's --recovery t1=FILE (robofast.testing.rehearsal).

powercycle SWITCHES A REAL OUTLET (JDE 2026-11-10: panel and inst) through the PDU server of t1_pdu.json on 127.0.0.1:11131, which the operator starts with --hardware (docs/recovery.md, 'Running the PDU servers'). Switch ids are that config's outlets in order: 1 = panel (the mount controller), 2 = inst (the Andor camera).

telescope: reconnect, restart (PWI), home, then powercycle(panel). Cycling panel cuts the mount controller (encoders lost): PWI is stopped first and started after (legacy's constraint; requires_pwi_stop), then robofast reconnects PWI to the mount (MountConnect, MotorsEnable) and homes it; the rung counts only once the mount is homed (the PWI server needs allow_find_home).

camera: reconnect, then powercycle(inst): the camera alone (the Andor camera). Its cooler is set again on the reconnect (the site config's cooling entry). A camera that still answers colder than camera_warm_above is not cut off; one that does not answer is.

Guards on every cycle: the telescope parked (requires_parked), the camera idle, at most one cycle a night per device (max_powercycles) and min_interval s apart, plus the PDU server's own cycle outlets and min_cycle_interval.

The hooks (/usr/local/bin/minerva-pwi T VERB: restart, stop or start PWI on the telescope's PC through the site gateway; exit 0 only once PWI answers, for restart and start) are the site deployment's, outside this repository (docs/recovery.md, 'The restart hook').
